# US Census Demographics — Cloud-Native Mirror

> Nationwide U.S. Census Bureau statistics as GeoParquet + PMTiles with STAC
> metadata: ACS 2020–2024 5-year indicators at block group (242,298), tract
> (85,184), county (3,235), state (56), ZCTA (33,791), place (32,612) and
> congressional district (441, 119th Congress) level, plus 2020 Decennial
> Census counts for all 8,174,955 census blocks. Every ACS estimate carries
> its margin of error (`*_moe`, 90% confidence); headline statistics carry a
> reliability coefficient of variation (`*_cv`). CC0-1.0; data.census.gov is
> the authoritative source.

Base URL: https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/

Read [AGENTS.md](https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/AGENTS.md)
first: join keys (GEOIDs nest by prefix: state 2 / congressional district 4 /
county 5 / ZCTA 5 / place 7 / tract 11 / block group 12 / block 15 chars),
MOE math, and the quirks that produce silently wrong answers. Each geography
is a sub-catalog with its own AGENTS.md, and each collection has one too,
with tested queries and a README.md documenting every column.

## Shape: seven geographies, five themes

Every ACS geography is a sub-catalog of themed collections, and the themes are
the same everywhere — income, people, housing, connectivity, wellbeing — so
one theme is one file of 23–34 columns instead of 112.

- block-groups/bg-{income,people,housing,connectivity} — no wellbeing chunk:
  health insurance, disability, nativity and income by race are not published
  below tract
- tracts/tract-{income,people,housing,connectivity,wellbeing}
- counties/county-{income,people,housing,connectivity,wellbeing} + counties
- states/state-{…} + states
- zctas/zcta-{…} + zctas
- places/place-{…} + places
- congressional-districts/cd-{…} + congressional-districts
- blocks/state_fips=*/<fips>.parquet — 2020 P.L. 94-171 block counts,
  hive-partitioned by state FIPS

The five coarse-or-sparse geographies add a sixth collection carrying all 112
columns on the same rows, for a question that crosses themes.

## Data URLs (the wide tables differ)

    <base>/<group>/<cid>/<cid>.parquet    every themed chunk, e.g.
                                          counties/county-income/county-income.parquet
    <base>/<group>/<group>.parquet        the five wide tables, e.g.
                                          counties/counties.parquet

A wide table's collection.json, README.md and styles/ live in
`<group>/<group>/`, but its GeoParquet and PMTiles stayed one directory up, so
every published data URL keeps working. `counties/counties/counties.parquet`
is a 404. PMTiles sit beside each parquet with the same stem, and the vector
layer name is always the collection id.

## Query patterns (DuckDB)

INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
-- national, no download:
SELECT state, median(median_hh_income) FROM
'https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/block-groups/bg-income/bg-income.parquet'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
-- one theme at a coarse geography (23-34 columns instead of 112):
SELECT geoid, name, median_hh_income FROM
'https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/counties/county-income/county-income.parquet'
WHERE state = 'CA' ORDER BY median_hh_income DESC LIMIT 5;
-- every column of one row, from the wide table (note: no second directory):
SELECT * EXCLUDE (geometry, bbox) FROM
'https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/counties/counties.parquet'
WHERE geoid = '06075';
-- one state's blocks via hive partition (name columns; SELECT * returns raw WKB):
SELECT geoid, pop_total, housing_units FROM
'https://data.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/blocks/state_fips=29/29.parquet' LIMIT 5;
-- chunks at one geography join 1:1 on geoid; roll blocks up to block groups
-- with substr(geoid,1,12); reach a row's state with substr(geoid,1,2).
-- all 52 block partitions as one table needs object listing, so use the S3 endpoint
-- (anonymous) — a state_fips=*/*.parquet glob over https://data.source.coop/ returns 404:
SET s3_region='us-west-2';
SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet(
's3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog/blocks/state_fips=*/*.parquet',
hive_partitioning=true);
-- filter cheaply with the bbox covering struct (it has row-group stats; string columns do not):
-- WHERE bbox.xmin < east AND bbox.xmax > west AND bbox.ymin < north AND bbox.ymax > south

Treat `*_cv` > 0.40 as unreliable; never sum medians across geographies; MOEs
add in quadrature. ZCTAs nest in nothing and `state` is NULL on all 33,791
rows, so a prefix join from a ZCTA returns wrong rows rather than no rows;
places do not tile the country and must never be summed to a total;
congressional districts are the 119th Congress and are not comparable to an
earlier one. PMTiles coarse zooms are a coarser census geography, not the
collection's own — counties at z0–z5, tracts in the middle, carrying the
Census Bureau's own estimates for those geographies — except at county, state
and congressional-district level, which are real polygons at every zoom. Use
the GeoParquet for statistics and check the zoom before reading a tiled
feature as a block group, tract, ZCTA or place.

Source repository: https://github.com/portolan-mirrors/us-census-catalog
